## Purpose

title: kda: use natural exp in the token-parallel intra-chunk kernel
body:
## What
In `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_intra_token_parallel`, apply the gate as `b_kj * exp(b_g - b_gj)` (natural exp) instead of `b_kj * exp2(b_g - b_gj)` (base-2).

## Why
The non-token-parallel path in `fla/kda.py` applies the same gate decay as `b_k * exp(b_g - b_gn[None, :])` (natural exp). The two paths compute the same quantity and must agree, so the token-parallel kernel was using the wrong base. The KDA gate `g` is in the natural-log domain (derived from `A_log = log(A)`), so the decay factor is `exp(g_i - g_j)`; `exp2` introduces a spurious `log2(e)` factor in the exponent.

The error is small and KDA models that run with `safe_gate` clamp the gate range and further mask the discrepancy, so it went unnoticed.

## Scope
One-line numerical fix in a shared fla module. Uses `exp` from `fla.op` to match the non-parallel path exactly.

## Summary

This PR supports bounded prefill admission waves for chunked prefill.

The policy works as follows:

- When the resident decode batch reaches `max_num_seqs`, do not reserve

MiniMax-M3's sparse attention runs a lightning-indexer pass in every sparse layer

title: feat: Add DeepSeek V4 SWA recompute
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek V4 keeps a FULL cache containing compressed C4/C128 and indexer state, plus a sliding-window attention (SWA) cache backed by a smaller KV pool. When this pool evicts the trailing SWA pages while the FULL prefix survives, the prefix cannot be reused directly and may fall back to cold prefill. This PR retains the FULL hit and recomputes only the bounded trailing dependency window needed to rebuild SWA.

The feature is disabled by default and enabled with `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RECOMPUTE_WINDOW=1`.

- Compute a page-aligned recompute window from the sliding window `W`, number of layers `N`, and KV page size:
